title: Ray Diagrams
page_title: Ray Diagrams | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Physics Revision Notes 2021

blocks.name: Features of Ray Diagrams
blocks.definition: Define and use the terms focal length, principal axis and principal focus (focal point)

blocks.md:
- Ray diagrams can be described using the following terms:

  - principal axis
  - principal focus, or focal point
  - focal length
- The principal axis is defined as:
**A line which passes through the centre of a lens**
- The principal focus, or focal point, is defined as:
**The point at which rays of light travelling parallel to the principal axis intersect the principal axis and converge or the point at which diverging rays appear to proceed**
**The distance between the centre of the lens and the principal focus**

blocks.name: Converging & diverging lenses
blocks.definition: Describe the action of thin converging and thin diverging lenses on a parallel beam of light

blocks.md:
- A lens is a piece of equipment that forms an image by [refracting light](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/physics/cie/23/revision-notes/3-waves/3-2-light/3-2-3-refraction-of-light/?_ai=internal-linking)
- There are two types of lens:

  - converging
  - diverging

- In a converging lens, parallel rays of light are brought to a focus

  - This point is called the **principal focus**

- This lens is sometimes referred to as a **convex** lens
- The distance from the lens to the principal focus is called the **focal length**

  - This depends on how **curved** the lens is
  - The **more** curved the lens, the **shorter** the focal length

blocks.alt: Diagram of a converging lens showing parallel rays converging to the principal focus on the right, with the focal length marked by a green arrow from the centre of the converging lens to the principal focus.
blocks.caption: The focal length is the distance from the lens to the principal focus

blocks.md:
- In a diverging lens, parallel rays of light are made to diverge (spread out) from a point

  - This lens is sometimes referred to as a **concave** lens
- The principal focus is now the point from which the rays appear to diverge from

blocks.alt: Diagram of a diverging lens showing parallel rays spreading out at the diverging lens. The extensions of the diverging rays meet at the principal focus on the axis, with focal length marked from the principal focus to the centre of the diverging lens.
blocks.caption: Parallel rays from a diverging lens appear to come from the principal focus

blocks.md: - In diagrams, the following symbols are often used to represent each type of lens:

blocks.alt: Diagram comparing convex and concave lens symbols. A double‑headed arrow is used to represent a convex lens, and a Y‑shaped arrow is used to represent a concave lens.
blocks.caption: Concave and convex lens symbols

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: To remember which lens is converging or diverging, think of the following: Con**v**ex lens = Con**v**erging. You need to be able to describe how the lenses affect the light rays.
